To express temporary location or state
The books are on the table.
I’ll be at the airport at 6.
The cake was made by her.
Where will you be tomorrow night?
I’ll be at home, finishing my book.

Why are you being so negative?

No, I’ll be studying for my exam.

It was already 10 PM. Maria was tired but still working. Her team was being very demanding that week. She was supposed to be home by 8, but things got delayed. When she finally left the office, it was raining and she was cold. Her apartment is far from downtown, so she knew it would be a long ride. Still, she was grateful to be employed.

Choose the most natural use of "be":
I’ll (stay / be / remain) there until 6 PM.
The room (has / is / stays) very dark without the lights.
She (be / has been / is) upset since morning.
Rewrite using “be” instead of verbs in parentheses:
She (ficou) very sad when she heard the news.
I (estou) here now, but I (vou estar) at school later.
B: I know. My boss ___ being difficult again.
